questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make a perfect cup of coffee at home
Why tea is healthier than coffee
How coffee is grown in Africa and Asia
The history of coffee in Britain
questions.why: Sam says they'll be looking into the history of coffee in Britain.

questions.q: What does Neil like about coffee?
options: It helps him sleep well at night
Its smell, and it wakes him up
It is cheaper than other drinks
It helps him stop eating snacks
questions.why: Neil mentions 'that lovely smell' and says it wakes him up and gets him ready to face the world.

questions.q: What was the first coffee in Britain like?
options: It took months to arrive and tasted awful
It was sweet and very expensive to buy
It came from farms in the south of England
It was only drunk by the king and queen
questions.why: Sam says it took months to arrive by sea, was made by boiling raw beans, and apparently tasted awful.

questions.q: What happened after London's first coffee shop opened in 1652?
options: The government quickly banned coffee
People said coffee made them sleepy
Over eighty more opened in ten years
Most people still preferred tea
questions.why: Neil says within a decade over eighty new coffee shops had opened in the City of London alone.

questions.q: Why did tea replace coffee as the fashionable drink by the 1800s?
options: Coffee became illegal in Britain
Coffee shops became too crowded
Tea was much cheaper to import
Partly as Queen Victoria drank it
questions.why: Sam says tea replaced coffee partly because it was drunk by Queen Victoria.

questions.q: According to Judith Hawley, why did the Temperance Movement support coffee taverns?
options: To keep working men out of the pub
To make money from selling coffee
To give rich people a place to meet
To help coffee farmers in Yemen
questions.why: She says they sponsored coffee taverns 'to try to wean working men off going to the pub for lunch'.

questions.q: What two directions does Judith Hawley see for coffee today?
options: Hot coffee or cold coffee drinks
Big chains, or quality handmade coffee
Coffee at home or coffee at work
Coffee from Africa or from South America
questions.why: She describes corporate coffee chains on one hand and Fairtrade, microlot, artisanal coffee on the other.

questions.q: What does the Fairtrade scheme do?
options: It sells coffee only in small, trendy shops
It makes coffee cheaper for customers
It guarantees farmers a fair price
It grows coffee on very small farms
questions.why: Sam says it guarantees a fair price for coffee producers in South America, Africa and Asia.
